body: Trauma Center: Under the Knife is Atlus' Nintendo DS medical thriller combining stylus-controlled operations with a story about young surgeon Derek Stiles. A new artificial disease called GUILT brings him into the work of the organisation Caduceus, while his unusual Healing Touch provides an exceptional ability under pressure. Story scenes introduce the people and the next medical emergency before the player moves to the operating table. The handheld's touchscreen becomes the working surface, turning a list of instruments into a set of precise actions that must keep a patient alive.

Operations take place from above the affected area, with tool icons arranged around the touchscreen. The stylus makes incisions, removes objects, closes wounds and performs other procedures appropriate to the instrument selected. A time limit and the patient's vital signs keep the sequence under pressure. Reading the briefing and following instructions help establish what needs to be treated, but recognising the next action quickly becomes essential once several problems compete for attention. Accuracy matters because a careless movement can make the patient's condition harder to stabilise.

Conversations and portraits connect the operations with Derek's colleagues and his responsibilities as a doctor. The science-fiction threat then pushes the procedures beyond familiar injuries, turning some encounters with GUILT into elaborate medical confrontations. The Healing Touch provides a special response when the ordinary pace becomes overwhelming. The combination gives the touchscreen actions a clear dramatic purpose: selecting an instrument is part of an attempt to save a particular person. A successful operation resolves both a demanding sequence of movements and the immediate crisis established by the story.
